title: Finite-free ordinary scalar extension on unbounded cochain complexes
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, finite extensions $E,L$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, an embedding $\iota:E\to L$ and any scheme $W$. Let $R_W,S_W$, the actual ordinary scalar functor, its termwise complex functor, and its universal derived counit be those of [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison]. Then the ordinary scalar functor preserves countable products; its complex functor sends every flat-term K-flat complex to a flat-term K-flat complex in the sense of [lem-pur-integral-operations-well-defined], [def-pc-kflat-complex]; and its universal derived counit is an isomorphism on every unbounded complex. In particular the counit claim requires no flatness of the input complex. The statement concerns completed coefficient sheaves, and makes no flatness assertion for ramified finite quotient inclusions.

source.place: Tag 03EK, section-tensor-product, and sites-cohomology.tex, Tag 06YY (K-flat change of rings); finite-free exactness, products and derived counit of Steps 4, 6 and 7 of lem-weil-scalar-pullback-strict-cone-naturality.

proof.text: Finite freeness identifies the restriction of the scalar functor with a finite direct sum of identity functors. The coordinate inverse to each product comparison uses a finite sum over the basis index, so ordinary scalar extension preserves countable products. Restriction creates kernels and cokernels and reflects isomorphisms; the same finite-power comparison proves exactness. In Lean use the proved scalarExactProducts helper of the finite-free quotient Roos module, with the product-form free basis converted to a finite biproduct.

proof.text: Apply the change-of-rings theorem with independent site and coefficient universes to the recorded ordinary scalar functor and its object/map specification. Transport termwise flatness through the site-sheaf tensor-right comparison. Its conclusion is exactly the good-complex property.

proof.text: Exactness implies that termwise scalar extension sends every quasi-isomorphism to a quasi-isomorphism. Its composite with the target localization therefore inverts all quasi-isomorphisms. The universal left-derived counit is invertible by the general localization criterion Functor.isIso_of_isLeftDerivedFunctor_of_inverts; evaluate this natural isomorphism on every complex. The model counit is definitionally the published scalar counit.

theorem finiteFreeScalarCochainProperties (W : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.{t}) :
    PreservesLimitsOfShape (Discrete ℕ) (completedOrdinaryScalarExtension l E L ι W) ∧
    (∀ P : (integralOperationsGoodComplex l E W).FullSubcategory,
      integralOperationsGoodComplex l L W
        ((completedOrdinaryScalarComplex l E L ι W).obj P.obj)) ∧
    (∀ P : CochainComplex (integralTowerModules l E W) ℤ,
      IsIso (completedScalarCounit l E L ι W P))
